Chinchero Archaeological Park

Agricultural terraces below the upper plaza

Current ratingsOpening hoursView the place on the map
Nearby places

Explore

Inca terraces descend from the monumental core toward cultivated land. Their retaining walls make a strong contrast with the painted church on the upper plaza. The park visit is best understood as a sequence of occupied, ceremonial and agricultural spaces.

Planning your visit

60–90 min · Allow this time for the visit itself. Add travel, admission queues and any scheduled tour separately.

What to look for

Agricultural terraces below the upper plaza

Keep the top of the terrace wall and the cultivated ground behind it in the same frame. This avoids mistaking an agricultural retaining wall for a room wall.

History and local experience

Look beyond the monumental core to fields outside it. The change from formal stonework to cultivated ground keeps the connection between the settlement and Andean agriculture visible.

Walking route

  1. Parque Arqueológico de Chinchero, Urubamba
  2. Enter at the archaeological checkpoint, cross the upper plaza and follow the designated path to the terrace viewpoints.
  3. Return to the settlement on the signed trail rather than crossing cultivated plots.

Before you go

Visitor questions

How do I reach the site?

Enter at the archaeological checkpoint, cross the upper plaza and follow the designated path to the terrace viewpoints. Return to the settlement on the signed trail rather than crossing cultivated plots.

What should I look for here?

Keep the top of the terrace wall and the cultivated ground behind it in the same frame. This avoids mistaking an agricultural retaining wall for a room wall.

Where can I verify access and admission?

The site authority sets the open sectors and the last admission. Confirm these with the control post, particularly on days with rain or maintenance.
